lean_engine_validation.method: grammar_engine_lean.enumerate_lean's by_complexity_counts compared exactly against grammar_engine.enumeration_counts (the frozen, already-used engine) for every complexity level small enough for the frozen engine to finish in reasonable time.

bug_found_and_fixed_during_validation.description: First validation attempt (before the fix) showed 4 of 7 cases MISMATCH, with the lean engine consistently OVER-counting (registering entries the original engine correctly deduplicated as algebraic duplicates).
bug_found_and_fixed_during_validation.root_cause: IEEE754 -0.0 == 0.0 by Python float value equality (which grammar_engine.enumerate_expressions relies on via direct tuple `in` membership), but repr(-0.0) == '-0.0' != repr(0.0) == '0.0'. The lean engine's hash-of-repr dedup key therefore treated a -0.0-containing fingerprint and an otherwise-identical 0.0-containing fingerprint as DIFFERENT values, under-deduplicating. Concrete example found: floor(mu) and pow(log(log(m)),N) both fingerprint to an all-zero (with alternating sign) tuple on the sample grid and must dedup as one value; before the fix they did not.
bug_found_and_fixed_during_validation.fix: grammar_engine_lean._normalize_fp_value maps -0.0 to 0.0 (and passes None through) before repr()-based hashing; both floats already came from grammar_engine.numeric_fingerprint's own round(float(v), 9), so no precision is lost by this normalization.
bug_found_and_fixed_during_validation.verification_after_fix: All 7 cases MATCH exactly, including the largest (427,569 forms at complexity 7 of the fb3_unsigned_m3_and_enum_unsigned_m3 pack).
